newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Court orders gambling broadcast ban review.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Court orders gambling broadcast ban review.

text.p: The Supreme Court Monday set aside a ruling that upheld as constitutional a federal law barring the broadcast of radio and television advertisements for casino gambling.

The justices sent the case back to a U.S. appeals court for further review in light of a Supreme Court decision in May that struck down a state ban on advertising of retail liquor prices for violating constitutional free-speech rights.

The law bars television and radio stations licensed by the Federal Communications Commission from broadcasting advertisements for any "lottery, gift enterprise or similar scheme offering prizes dependent ... upon lot or chance."

The law had been challenged by a number of television and radio stations in New Orleans, which sought to broadcast ads for casino gambling in Louisiana and Mississippi. Casino gambling is legal in the two states.

The appeals court upheld the law on the grounds that the law advances the government's interest in discouraging public participation in gambling and helps enforce anti-gambling policies in those states which have them.

Although the ruling was a victory for the federal government, the Justice Department still urged the Supreme Court to send the case back for further consideration in light of the high court's decision in May.
But Justice Department lawyers said their request does not mean the appeals court decision was wrong or that the Supreme Court ruling renders the gambling broadcast ban unconstitutional.
